chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAllān, from Jaʿfar ibn Yūnus, that his father wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
About the junub applying dye, or becoming junub while he is dyed; so he wrote: I do not like that for him.
Thus this report came explicitly indicating karahah, not prohibition.

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness in legal usage, short of prohibition
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: I do not like it; an expression indicating disapproval
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye, especially henna or similar coloring

ai.seo_question: Is it prohibited or merely disliked for a junub to apply dye or remain dyed in the state of janabah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on a junub using dye or entering janabah while already dyed. The Imam عليه السلام expresses disapproval, and the text explicitly clarifies that the ruling indicates karahah rather than prohibition.
